input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 is the only inspection right running against the Company. It has no frequency limit at all, so HDI could inspect repeatedly; unlimited audits fail even the fallback (once per year), which is a material term. The minimal cure inserts a once-per-year cap; the remaining fallback terms are already satisfied or bettered by the existing drafting (30 days' prior written notice exceeds the 15-day fallback, and HDI bears its inspection costs unconditionally, which is better than a 10% underpayment shift). With the cap added the clause sits at our fallback. Shortfalls versus preferred, noted only in rationale: the inspection is by HDI's General Manager rather than an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (though Section 8.2 confidentiality binds HDI), there is no express off-site or no-systems-access language (the right is limited to records, not systems), and there is no 5% underpayment cost-shift.
